note.text:
Vitamins are micronutrients needed for growth and health. Two groups:
• Fat-soluble: A, D, E, K (stored in the body).
• Water-soluble: B group and C (not stored; needed every day; easily lost in cooking water).
Sources and functions:
• A: carrots, palm oil, liver, mangoes, green leaves; eyesight in dim light, healthy skin. Lack: night blindness.
• B1 (thiamine): whole grains, beans, groundnuts; releasing energy. Lack: beriberi.
• C: oranges, guavas, pawpaw, green leaves; healthy gums, healing wounds, absorbing iron. Lack: scurvy.
• D: sunlight on the skin, fish oil, eggs; strong bones and teeth. Lack: rickets.
• K: green leafy vegetables; blood clotting.
Cook vegetables quickly in little water, with the lid on, to keep vitamin C.

worked_example.problem: How should {v} be cooked to keep most of its vitamin C?
steps: Vitamin C dissolves in water and is destroyed by long heating.
Wash before cutting, cook quickly in a little water with the lid on, and serve at once.
worked_example.answer: Quickly, in little water, with a lid, and eaten at once.

questions.prompt: Match each vitamin to its function.

right.text: Vitamin C is found in oranges.
Vitamin D is made in the skin in sunlight.
Vitamin A helps us see in dim light.
Vitamin K helps blood to clot.

wrong.text: Vitamin C is a fat-soluble vitamin.
Long boiling in a lot of water keeps vitamin C.
wrong.explain: Long boiling destroys and washes away vitamin C.

wrong.text: Lack of vitamin D causes scurvy.
wrong.explain: Lack of vitamin D causes rickets; scurvy is lack of vitamin C.
